episode_title: How YouTube Growth Works with Sergey Ross

real_qa.q: How does YouTube algorithm prioritize viewer satisfaction compared to other social media platforms?
real_qa.r: YouTube's algorithm works primarily by looking at viewer satisfaction through multiple signals: how long people stay on the video, survey ratings at the end of videos, likes, shares, and replay moments of specific video sections. All these factors combine into a satisfaction score that determines if the video will perform. If the audience wants to watch it, the video is absolutely going to perform.

real_qa.q: What is the most important factor for YouTube video growth: production quality or video idea?
real_qa.r: Ideas are the most important thing by far on YouTube. Production quality, including lighting and background setup, ranks at the bottom of the priority list. What matters most is that people can see you clearly and hear you well. The real priority order is: ideas first, then packaging (intro, hook, storytelling structure, title, thumbnail), and production quality comes much later.
real_qa.requete: YouTube video ideas versus production quality importance

real_qa.q: Can small channels still grow on YouTube or is it only for established creators with large audiences?
real_qa.r: Small channels absolutely can grow. Right now subscribers matter much less than before, which gives opportunity for small creators with 100 or 200 subscribers to grow if they have great videos. The bad news is there is more competition, meaning higher demand for video quality in terms of title, intro, and content. Small channels need to create really great content to perform.

real_qa.q: What is the ideal length for podcast videos on YouTube?
real_qa.r: There is no set duration that works universally. By 2026, longer videos tend to perform better, but it depends on the idea, packaging, title, thumbnail, introduction, hook (usually 60 to 120 seconds), and storytelling. Video length could be 5 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes, or even 3 hours if people are willing to watch it and the content engages them.

real_qa.q: Should podcast video content on YouTube include a teaser intro or start with an engaging question?
real_qa.r: For interview format, you can test both approaches. A teaser should be 20 to 30 seconds, maximum 35 seconds. Alternatively, you can start with an engaging question followed by the guest introduction later, without a pre-cut teaser. The key is that the core idea of the episode must be interesting and match what the core audience cares about.
